note: Vocabularies of the global impact layer (docs/GLOBAL_IMPACT_METHODOLOGY.md §4-§7, §9, §10). Read by pipeline/global_impacts.py and scripts/import_impacts.py, and served with labels in global/impacts.json, global/regional_context.json and global/evidence_confidence.json. Nothing here is a score, a weight or an order of importance: every list is in the order the methodology states it.

domains.label: Energy
domains.definition: An energy system was interrupted or degraded: electricity, oil and gas, fuel supply or district energy.

domains.label: Civilian service
domains.definition: An essential civilian service other than energy was interrupted or degraded.

sectors.label: Electricity
sectors.definition: Generation, transmission, distribution or control of electric power.

sectors.label: Oil and gas
sectors.definition: Production, processing, refining or liquefaction of oil and natural gas.

sectors.label: Fuel supply
sectors.definition: Storage, distribution and retail supply of fuels to users.

sectors.label: District energy
sectors.definition: District heating or cooling supplied to buildings through a network.

sectors.label: Water
sectors.definition: Treatment and supply of drinking water.

sectors.label: Wastewater
sectors.definition: Collection and treatment of sewage and wastewater.

sectors.label: Desalination
sectors.definition: Production of fresh water from seawater or brackish water.

sectors.label: Healthcare
sectors.definition: Hospitals, emergency care and the services they depend on to treat patients.

sectors.label: Transport
sectors.definition: Public transport, rail, aviation and road services used by the public.

sectors.label: Municipal services
sectors.definition: Local government services such as emergency dispatch, waste collection and public administration.

technologies.label: Refining
technologies.definition: Processing of crude oil into fuels and other products.

technologies.label: LNG
technologies.definition: Liquefaction or regasification of natural gas.

technologies.label: Gas processing
technologies.definition: Treatment of natural gas before it is transported or used.

technologies.label: Fuel storage or distribution
technologies.definition: Storage and delivery of fuels to users, including retail stations.

technologies.label: Hydro generation
technologies.definition: Electricity generated from flowing or stored water.

technologies.label: Battery or grid storage
technologies.definition: Storage of electricity for later use on the grid.

technologies.label: Transmission
technologies.definition: High-voltage movement of electricity over long distances.

technologies.label: Distribution
technologies.definition: Delivery of electricity to homes and businesses.

technologies.label: Grid control
technologies.definition: The systems and staff that balance and operate a power grid.

technologies.label: Other energy
technologies.definition: An energy technology that fits none of the other entries, or more than one of them.

cause_families.label: Kinetic attack
cause_families.definition: A physical armed attack. Published for the country only, with no place, method or later status.

cause_families.label: Cyber
cause_families.definition: A disruption caused through computer systems or networks.

cause_families.label: Sabotage
cause_families.definition: Deliberate physical damage other than an armed attack. Published for the country only.

cause_families.label: Industrial or technical failure
cause_families.definition: An accident, equipment failure or operating error.

cause_families.label: Natural hazard
cause_families.definition: Weather, wildfire, flood, earthquake or another natural event.

cause_families.label: Supply shortfall
cause_families.definition: Not enough fuel, water or generation to meet demand.

cause_families.label: Civil disruption
cause_families.definition: A strike, protest or unrest that interrupted the service.

cause_families.label: Ordered by an authority
cause_families.definition: A service restricted or shut down by order of an authority (for example an exam-period or protest-period internet shutdown). Not a malicious incident: attribution is NOT_APPLICABLE and the record says who ordered it only as a source states.

cause_families.label: Cause not established
cause_families.definition: Public sources do not establish the cause.

country_cause_to_family.note: How a country system's `cause` relates to a cause family here. The country vocabulary is unchanged and nothing is migrated. A null family means that cause is never an impact record.

asset_class_to_technology.note: How a country system's `asset_class` relates to a sector and technology here. A separate field; nothing is migrated. A null means the class alone does not decide it and the record's own sources do.

cyber_mechanisms.label: Ransomware
cyber_mechanisms.definition: Systems were encrypted or locked and a ransom demanded.

cyber_mechanisms.label: Denial of service
cyber_mechanisms.definition: A service was flooded with traffic until it could not respond.

cyber_mechanisms.label: Unauthorised access
cyber_mechanisms.definition: Someone without permission entered systems; no further mechanism is reported.

cyber_mechanisms.label: IT outage affecting operations
cyber_mechanisms.definition: Business computer systems went down and operations stopped or slowed as a result.

cyber_mechanisms.label: Operational technology disruption
cyber_mechanisms.definition: Systems that control physical equipment were disrupted.

cyber_mechanisms.label: Supply chain compromise
cyber_mechanisms.definition: The disruption came through software or equipment from a supplier.

cyber_mechanisms.label: Malicious configuration change
cyber_mechanisms.definition: Settings were deliberately changed so that a service failed.

cyber_mechanisms.label: Destructive malware
cyber_mechanisms.definition: Malicious software built to damage systems or stop them working.

cyber_mechanisms.label: Service provider compromise
cyber_mechanisms.definition: The disruption came through an outside company that runs systems for the operator.

cyber_mechanisms.label: Cyber-physical disruption
cyber_mechanisms.definition: A cyber incident reported to have caused a physical effect.

cyber_mechanisms.label: Mechanism not reported
cyber_mechanisms.definition: Sources call the incident cyber and do not say what kind.

digital_categories.label: Cyber
digital_categories.definition: A cyberattack: the cause, or a contributing cause, is malicious activity through computer systems.

digital_categories.label: IT failure
digital_categories.definition: Digitally triggered without malice, such as a faulty software update or a system failure. Not a cyberattack, and never counted as one.

source_roles.label: Operator
source_roles.definition: The company or body that runs the affected service.

source_roles.label: Government
source_roles.definition: A ministry, agency or official of a government.

source_roles.label: Regulator
source_roles.definition: The public body that oversees the sector.

source_roles.label: National cyber agency
source_roles.definition: A national computer emergency response team or cyber security agency.

source_roles.label: Court record
source_roles.definition: A filing or judgment of a court.

source_roles.label: Wire service
source_roles.definition: A news agency whose reports other outlets republish.

source_roles.label: News media
source_roles.definition: A news outlet reporting in its own name.

source_roles.label: Specialist press
source_roles.definition: Trade or technical press covering the sector.

source_roles.label: Cyber security firm
source_roles.definition: A security company reporting its own investigation.

source_roles.label: Dataset
source_roles.definition: A published data series or filing.

source_roles.label: Aggregator
source_roles.definition: A site that restates others' reporting. A discovery aid, never evidence on its own.

source_roles.label: Actor's own claim
source_roles.definition: A statement by a group claiming responsibility. A claim is not corroboration.

media.label: Web page
media.definition: An article, release or page on a website.

media.label: Dataset
media.definition: A published data file or data series.

media.label: Social media post
media.definition: A public post on a social platform. A medium, not a quality level.

social_tiers.label: Official account
social_tiers.definition: The official account of a government, regulator, operator or company, with identity established from the organisation's own site.

social_tiers.label: Recognised journalist or institution
social_tiers.definition: A recognised journalist or institution. Used for discovery and observation; material claims are corroborated.

social_tiers.label: Researcher account
social_tiers.definition: A reputable open-source researcher. A lead, never the sole evidence.

social_tiers.label: Unknown account
social_tiers.definition: An unknown or anonymous account. Discovery only, never cited as sole evidence.

claims.label: That it happened
claims.definition: The source supports that the disruption occurred.

claims.label: The effect
claims.definition: The source supports what the effect on the service was.

claims.label: Attribution
claims.definition: The source supports who is said to be responsible.

claims.label: AI involvement
claims.definition: The source ties AI to this incident.

attribution_statuses.label: Not applicable
attribution_statuses.definition: Not a malicious act, so there is nobody to attribute it to.

attribution_statuses.label: Not established
attribution_statuses.definition: Malicious or possibly malicious, with no credible public attribution.

attribution_statuses.label: Claimed
attribution_statuses.definition: An actor claimed responsibility. A claim is not corroboration.

attribution_statuses.label: Suspected
attribution_statuses.definition: A credible source names a likely actor without a firm attribution.

attribution_statuses.label: Assessed
attribution_statuses.definition: A government body, the victim or a technical investigator assesses that an actor was responsible.

attribution_statuses.label: Attributed
attribution_statuses.definition: A formal government or law-enforcement attribution, or several independent attributions that agree.

attribution_statuses.label: Disputed
attribution_statuses.definition: Credible sources attribute the incident differently, and the product does not choose.

actor_types.label: State
actor_types.definition: The source names a government or its forces.

actor_types.label: State-linked
actor_types.definition: The source describes a group as linked to a state. Linked is not controlled.

actor_types.label: Hacktivist
actor_types.definition: The source describes a politically motivated group.

actor_types.label: Criminal
actor_types.definition: The source describes a group acting for money.

actor_types.label: Insider
actor_types.definition: The source describes someone inside the affected organisation.

actor_types.label: Type not stated
actor_types.definition: The source names an actor without saying what kind.

actor_types.label: Other
actor_types.definition: The source describes an actor that fits none of the other types.

attribution_bases.label: A government
attribution_bases.definition: A government body made the attribution.

attribution_bases.label: Law enforcement
attribution_bases.definition: Police, prosecutors or a court made the attribution.

attribution_bases.label: The affected operator
attribution_bases.definition: The organisation that was affected made the attribution.

attribution_bases.label: A cyber security firm
attribution_bases.definition: A security company made the attribution from its own investigation.

attribution_bases.label: A researcher
attribution_bases.definition: An independent or academic researcher made the attribution.

attribution_bases.label: A media investigation
attribution_bases.definition: A news organisation made the attribution from its own reporting.

attribution_bases.label: The actor's own claim
attribution_bases.definition: The actor said it was responsible.

ai_statuses.label: None reported
ai_statuses.definition: No source ties AI to this incident.

ai_statuses.label: Claimed
ai_statuses.definition: Someone claims AI was involved, without an official or technical finding.

ai_statuses.label: Suspected
ai_statuses.definition: A credible source says AI may have been involved.

ai_statuses.label: Assessed
ai_statuses.definition: An official or technical investigator assesses that AI was involved.

ai_statuses.label: Confirmed
ai_statuses.definition: The operator, a government investigation or the vendor's own report states that AI was involved.

ai_relations.label: AI-assisted
ai_relations.definition: An attacker used AI tooling. This does not mean AI caused the outage.

ai_relations.label: AI in operations
ai_relations.definition: An AI system used in operations made the erroneous decision, or an AI service the operation relied on failed.

ai_roles.label: Attacker assistance
ai_roles.definition: AI helped an attacker in a way the source does not specify further.

ai_roles.label: Generated deceptive messages
ai_roles.definition: AI was used to write or voice messages meant to deceive people.

ai_roles.label: Generated malicious code
ai_roles.definition: AI was used to write malicious code or scripts.

ai_roles.label: Automated the attack
ai_roles.definition: AI was used to run steps of the attack automatically.

ai_roles.label: AI system failure
ai_roles.definition: An AI system used to run the service made a wrong decision or failed.

ai_roles.label: AI-generated configuration or code
ai_roles.definition: Settings or code produced by AI were deployed and caused the failure.

ai_roles.label: AI service outage
ai_roles.definition: An AI service the operation relied on was unavailable.

ai_roles.label: Other
ai_roles.definition: A role the source describes that fits none of the other entries.

ai_roles.label: Role not stated
ai_roles.definition: The source ties AI to the incident without saying what it did.

context_types.label: Shipping, in aggregate
context_types.definition: A dated statement that shipping in the region is restricted or disrupted, in aggregate.

context_types.label: Trade, in aggregate
context_types.definition: A dated statement about total trade volumes.

context_types.label: Supply, in aggregate
context_types.definition: A dated statement about total energy supply.

context_types.label: Market response
context_types.definition: A dated statement about prices or markets. A market movement is not infrastructure loss.

context_types.label: Reserve action
context_types.definition: A dated statement about the use of strategic reserves.

context_types.label: Policy response
context_types.definition: A dated statement about a government or international policy response.

context_types.label: Civilian and environmental effects
context_types.definition: A dated statement about broad civilian or environmental consequences.

record_kinds.label: Disruption
record_kinds.definition: A real interruption or degradation of a service, non-trivial in scale or duration.

record_kinds.label: ATTEMPT — NO REPORTED SERVICE DISRUPTION
record_kinds.definition: A clearly documented attempt with no reported effect on the service. Never counted with disruptions.

absence_words.label: Unknown
absence_words.definition: Researched; public sources do not say.

absence_words.label: Withheld
absence_words.definition: Known and deliberately not published under the scope rules.

absence_words.label: No public evidence
absence_words.definition: Researched; no public source was found.

absence_words.label: Source inaccessible
absence_words.definition: A source exists and could not be opened.

null_means: Not applicable. A null is never a zero, and a zero is never written for something unknown.

inclusion_bases.label: Emergency declaration
inclusion_bases.definition: An official emergency or formal incident declaration tied to the disruption.

inclusion_bases.label: Large population affected
inclusion_bases.definition: A service interruption affecting a large population, customer base or region, in the source's own figure and unit.

inclusion_bases.label: Stated power or output loss
inclusion_bases.definition: A material loss of power, load, generation or fuel output stated by an operator, regulator or government.

inclusion_bases.label: National or regional service lost
inclusion_bases.definition: Loss or severe degradation of a national or regional service.

inclusion_bases.label: Sustained disruption
inclusion_bases.definition: An essential service disrupted for days, or repeatedly over weeks.

inclusion_bases.label: Industrial or energy output interrupted
inclusion_bases.definition: A material interruption of industrial or energy output.

effect_specificity.label: Quantified
effect_specificity.definition: A source gives a figure for the effect.

effect_specificity.label: Described
effect_specificity.definition: A source describes a concrete effect without a figure.

effect_specificity.label: General terms only
effect_specificity.definition: Sources report disruption without saying what it was.

geographic_precision.label: Country
geographic_precision.definition: Recorded for the country as a whole.

geographic_precision.label: First-level region
geographic_precision.definition: Recorded for a state, province or equivalent. Never finer.

geographic_precision.label: Several countries
geographic_precision.definition: One event that affected more than one country.

geographic_scopes.label: National
geographic_scopes.definition: The source describes the effect as nationwide.

geographic_scopes.label: Regional
geographic_scopes.definition: The source describes the effect as covering part of the country.

geographic_scopes.label: Several regions
geographic_scopes.definition: The source describes the effect as covering several regions of the country.

geographic_scopes.label: Local
geographic_scopes.definition: The source describes the effect as limited to one community or operator.

geographic_scopes.label: Several countries
geographic_scopes.definition: The source describes the effect as crossing borders.

date_precision.label: Month
date_precision.definition: The sources give the month only.

date_precision.label: Year
date_precision.definition: The sources give the year only.

affected_qualifiers.definition: The source gives the figure without qualification.

affected_qualifiers.label: about
affected_qualifiers.definition: The source gives the figure as approximate.

affected_qualifiers.label: at least
affected_qualifiers.definition: The source gives the figure as a minimum.

affected_qualifiers.label: up to
affected_qualifiers.definition: The source gives the figure as a maximum.

publication_policies.label: Standard
publication_policies.definition: Published at country or first-level-region precision.

publication_policies.label: Country level only
publication_policies.definition: Published for the country only, with no place, operator, method, headline or later status. Every attack or sabotage record is.

link_states.label: Reachable
link_states.definition: The page loaded at the last automated check.

link_states.label: Redirected
link_states.definition: The address now leads to a different address.

link_states.label: Checker refused
link_states.definition: The site refused the automated checker. This does not mean the page is gone.

link_states.label: Not found
link_states.definition: The page was not found at the last check.

link_states.label: Error
link_states.definition: The check failed for a technical reason.

link_states.label: Deleted
link_states.definition: The post or page was removed by its author or platform. A corroborated claim stands.

link_states.label: Archived copy
link_states.definition: The original is gone and an archived copy is cited.

link_states.label: Not link-checked
link_states.definition: No automated check has been recorded for this address.

review_roles.label: Evidence
review_roles.definition: Opened the sources and checked identity, date, country, effect and every figure.

review_roles.label: Attribution and source
review_roles.definition: Checked what each source supports, the attribution, and the AI and social media checks.

review_roles.label: Safety and abstraction
review_roles.definition: Checked precision, abstraction, technical detail, status wording and personal data.

dispute_about.label: Whether it happened
dispute_about.definition: Credible sources disagree about whether the disruption occurred.

dispute_about.label: What the effect was
dispute_about.definition: Credible sources disagree about the effect on the service.

dispute_about.label: What caused it
dispute_about.definition: Credible sources disagree about the cause. Evidence confidence for the event itself is unchanged.

source_date_bases.label: Undated page
source_date_bases.definition: The page carries no date of its own (a running timeline, an agency landing page). It is cited without a date and earns nothing for being reported at the time.

importance_wording.note: What the gate reads as a claim about an asset's size or importance in an impact record's summary or effect. Not a vocabulary: a word list. 'always' is refused wherever it stands; a word of 'before_asset_noun' is refused directly before an asset noun or with at most 'words_between' words between; 'only' is refused with an asset noun among the next 'only_within_words' words; an allowed phrase is read as absent. Asset nouns also match with -s or -es.

route_wording_allowed.note: Phrases in which 'tanker' is a road vehicle delivering water or fuel, allowed in an impact record. Every other shipping, strait or route word is still refused there.
